knowledge_point.title: Solving for One Coefficient in a Linear Combination

question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $k$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{a}_{1}+k{a}_{2} & =0 \\ 3\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+k\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ k\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}-3\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ k\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ -12\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the final equation above, we can tell that $k=-6.$ This value satisfies every component.
